intended_object: The composed adversary matrix of Belovs–Lee, Definition 19, here for Boolean cube inputs. For an outer adversary matrix Γ_f on {0,1}^α and inner matrices M_i on {0,1}^β, it is (Γ_f ∘ M)[x,y] = Γ_f[g̃(x), g̃(y)] · ∏_i \hat{M_i}[x^i, y^i]. Here g̃(x)_i = g_i(x^i) and \hat N = N + ‖N‖·I. I took this from the docstring, the module docs and the `compose_apply` lemma.
explanation:
`compose` is the general `composeE` applied to the currying equivalence `cubeBlocks α β : ((α × β) → Bool) ≃ (α → β → Bool)`. `composeE` defines entry (x, y) as Γf(tilde x, tilde y) · ∏_i hat(M i)(x_i, y_i), with tilde x = (g_i(x_i))_i and hat N = N + ‖N‖ • 1 (the operator norm, from the `Matrix.Norms.L2Operator` scope). This is exactly the textbook composed adversary matrix. It allows a different inner function g_i and a different inner matrix for each block, which is the usual general form.

On generality: the library itself provides the general version, `composeE`, over any block decomposition `Z ≃ (α → Y)` with an arbitrary finite inner alphabet. This declaration is the explicitly labelled "uniform-alphabet" Boolean cube special case of it, kept so that existing statements stay as they were. A convenience specialization of a general definition that is already in the library is not a narrowing of the notion. The outer domain is `α → Bool` because the composed functions take Boolean values, which the construction needs.

Mathlib has no matching notion of adversary matrices or their composition.
